issues.failure_explanation: The skeleton identity \eqref{eq:1st_term_reformulated} (likewise the heuristic \eqref{eq:motivation_J_identity} and the multi-D \eqref{eq:md_error_identity}) keeps only the t=0 and t=T terms and the interior jump terms; the lateral contribution \int_{\partial\Omega\times(0,T)}(\mathbf f(u_{\theta^*})-\mathbf f(\tilde u_h))\sgn(u_{\theta^*}-\tilde u_h)\cdot n_x (with \tilde u_h=0 near \partial\Omega) is dropped without comment. The only justification offered is supp u(\cdot,t)\subset\Omega, which constrains the exact solution, not the network minimizer. The loss \eqref{eq:loss_func} penalizes only the initial trace (L_{bc} at t=0); no term constrains the trace of u_{\theta^*} on \partial\Omega\times(0,T), and the one-sided family J_{ent}(v;k_h)\le Ch yields no lower bound on this lateral flux (the candidate bounds are circular, involving \|v(T)\|_1 itself). Concretely, since the weak/entropy formulations \eqref{eq:weak_formulation}/\eqref{eq:entropy_solution} use test functions compactly supported in \Omega\times[0,T), boundary-inflow functions (e.g., an admissible shock entering through \partial\Omega with zero initial data) are also 'entropy solutions' of the same IVP, and by the paper's own competitor estimates they admit network approximations with loss O(h) while having O(1) final-time L^1 error from the compactly supported solution. Hence the loss as defined cannot distinguish the target solution, and the loss-to-error stability step underlying every error theorem is not closed.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated rate (h|\ln h|)^{1/2} is what results from balancing the strip-selection residual |\ln h|/M against Mh. But for a compound wave the shock borders a rarefaction fan emanating from the wave point, where |\nabla u|\sim(t-\tau_q)^{-1} (Assumption assump:piecewise_smooth(ii)). The shifted-interface transfer along that shock therefore contributes jL\int_\Gamma|\nabla u^\pm|ds \lesssim Mh|\ln h|, and the volume residual on the strip likewise carries the log — exactly as in the structurally identical shock-birth computation (\eqref{eq:shock_birth_shifted_trace_est}, \eqref{eq:shock_birth_volume_tilde}), where the same Mh|\ln h| term appears. Balancing |\ln h|/M with Mh|\ln h| gives M\sim h^{-1/2} and the rate h^{1/2}|\ln h|, which is strictly worse than the stated (h|\ln h|)^{1/2}. The paper's own main-1D appendix confirms this: it assigns compound pieces the estimate O(h^{1/2}|\ln h|), contradicting the standalone statement. The omitted proof cannot follow the cited strategy and yield the stated bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the bound as \|u_{\theta^*}(\cdot,T)-u(\cdot,T)\|_{L^1(\Omega)} \le C h^{1/2}|\ln h|, the rate the shifted-interface strategy actually delivers once the rarefaction-side (t-\tau_q)^{-1} gradient singularity along the shock is accounted for, matching the main-1D appendix.
issues.overall_effect: Only the standalone compound-wave theorem overstates the rate. The main 1D theorem (thm:main_1d) is unaffected because its appendix already uses the weaker O(h^{1/2}|\ln h|) for compound pieces, so no other result inherits the error.
